history.summary: North-facing granite Shiva temple at Ikkeri village, ~6 km south of Sagara (CSV town 'Shimoga' corrected: Shimoga is the district headquarters; the temple is at Ikkeri in Sagara taluk). Built during Keladi Nayaka rule in the 16th century; sources conflict on whether the capital shifted from Keladi to Ikkeri under Chaudappa Nayaka (r. 1499-1544) or c. 1560 — CONFLICT (verify). Ikkeri was the Nayaka capital for about 120 years; the temple is the only surviving vestige of that grandeur (the mud-and-timber palace and triple walls are lost). Architecture blends Kadamba, Hoysala, Chalukya, Vijayanagara and Nayaka elements: large mukha mandapa, open sukhanasi, garbha griha with a very high pedestal and 32 seated female figures around the Shivalinga (said to be self-manifested), white-spar Nandi shrine on axis, and effigies of three Keladi chiefs doing obeisance. Maintained by the ASI. Tradition holds it was desecrated by invaders and later renovated.

name: Aghoreshvara Temple, Ikkeri
town_description: Ikkeri is a heritage village in Sagara taluk of Shivamogga district, about 6 km south of Sagara town in Karnataka's Malnad region. The name means 'two streets' in Kannada. It was the second capital of the Keladi Nayakas for over a century after they shifted from Keladi; the town once had a grand palace and triple concentric fort walls, now lost. Today it is a quiet village whose main claim to fame is the ASI-maintained Aghoreshvara Temple, the sole surviving vestige of its former grandeur.
